questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study shipping-law and I also wanted to be at a university where the academic level was high.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. I used Erausmus University's website a lot. There is a lot of references to where you can find information about housing and social activities. Regarding Erasmus Travelgrant and preapproval (all those things in mobility online) i just followed the instructions in the mails that they sended me. Whenever I was unsure about anything on the Erasmus Univeristy side i just mailed the coordinator from Erasmus University.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got someone to pick up my key. I just texted the person over the app Going. Super easy. I would recommend doing the same if you are going to stay at Hatta building.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There where several different housing options. But be aware of the housing crisis in Rotterdam. There is a lot more students than there is housing available. Therefore, you either have to be very fast and lucky to get some housing through uni or you have to find something on the private housing market. I got lucky and got a room in the Hatta-building.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I shared a kitchen with two other guys. The kitchen was empty so we had to get kitchen stuff ourself. There where 4 hobs, 2 refrigerators, a sink and some empty closets to store kitchen stuff.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very convenient. The Hatta-building looks new and smart but its quite old on the inside and not very fancy at all.

What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was just emailed back and fourth with the student coordinator at ESL. Be aware that the courses get filled on a first come first served basis. So if there is a course you really want, then make sure to be early.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could mail the student coordinator from ESL.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was succesful. I got the ones I wished.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is based on first come first served - so be quick.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Research & Writing skills where completely useless and quite extensive. In this course they tell you a lot of academic stuff that you need for the master thesis but it is useless if you are just there as an exchange student. There way of teaching is also quite annoying. They just tell you to find a legal problem yourself and figure out what you want to research and how you want to do it yourself - so a lot of self studying.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level is quite high. Expect to use quite some time on school.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was different in the way that you have to hand in assignments during the course. These are graded as well on the same merrits as the masterstudents because the dont differentiate between exchange students and master students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Research & Writing Skills (Maritime and Transport Law), Law of the Sea, Commercial Contracts, and Transport Law

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Commercial Contracts and Transport Law. I liked the teachers.

questions.answer: Kitchen utilities.

questions.answer: Everything costs more or less the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I played basket at Baros and meet some really nice people. I can really recommend joining a sportsclub.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The sports center had all kinds of different sports. Basketball, volleyball, badminton etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get a sports pass to the Erasmus Sports Building. With it you can join all kinds of different teams and sessions.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Book a habour tour. You can also take the train to see Groningen, Amsterdam or Brussels.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. People are very friendly and similar to the people of Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports team. I am very happy that i joined Baros.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their very social culture. People are very keen to get a beer together after class.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Expect to spend quite a lot of time on the studies - you study with master students.
2) Join a sportsclub at the university
3) Rotterdam is a great city and a great hub from where you can travel to other big cities. On a weekend take the train to Paris, Amsterdam or Brussels.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a bike. It is so much easier to get around with a bike. Also the metro does not go all night like it does in Copenhagen and then you have to take a "night-bus" which is inconvenient.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning a lot of legal english and getting new friends. Also seeing the big industrial habour was a great experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The Research & Writing Skills course in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
